writeup.p: The velocity/knockback packet: entity id plus three motion shorts at x8000. The server emits it in three situations: EntityTrackerEntry broadcasts when a tracked entity's motion changes beyond a threshold (sendVelocityUpdates with lastTrackedEntityMotionX/Y/Z), EntityPlayer.attackEntityFrom sends it to the damaged player with the knockback vector, and explosions apply their push through S27. handleEntityVelocity overwrites the target entity's motion directly, which makes this the single most important clientbound packet for anti-knockback work.

EntityTrackerEntry compares the tracked entity's current motion to the last tracked values each tick and sends S12 when the delta crosses the threshold; EntityPlayer.attackEntityFrom sends the knockback vector straight to the damaged player's connection. On the client, handleEntityVelocity sets motionX/Y/Z = value / 8000.0 with no interpolation and no validation, so the packet is a direct write into the physics state that every movement check in the tick loop reads.

The most-handled clientbound packet in the corpus after S08. Four families: (1) cancel-or-scale anti-knockback (Memeware, Nekoware, Spicy, Tenacity, Rise 5.99 Custom); (2) per-anticheat timing games that cancel selectively or replay the knockback the way the anticheat expects (Rise 5.99 Vulcan/Tick Cancel/Stack/Follow First Tick/Ground, Sigma AACPush/AACFlag, the Rise 6.x ten-mode Velocity suite); (3) movement modules that consume S12 as a boost trigger (Rise 6.x GrimFlight TNT, WatchdogLongJump, WatchdogFireball, MatrixFlight, MineLandFlight, WatchdogBowLongJump; Rise 5.99 Fly Minemenclub and LongJump Hycraft/Vulcan; Sigma Fly; Tenacity FlightModule); (4) infrastructure: Rise's PingSpoofComponent buffers S12 in the velocity class, EntityTickComponent and ItemDamageComponent observe it, and Timer/Breaker/HurtCamera cancel it as collateral. November Recode 2.0's VelocityModule adds REDUCE, REVERSE, CANCEL and the per-anticheat GRIM, VULCAN, WATCHDOG and WATCHDOG_SAFE modes, with GRIM buffering S32 transactions and VULCAN cancelling the C0F echo.

The server recomputes knockback from attack packets and expects the resulting motion to appear in the player's reported positions over the next ticks. Cancelling S12 desyncs those reports, which is exactly what velocity checks measure, so the arms race is about timing: Tick Cancel and Stack modes cancel the first N velocity packets and let one through to satisfy the check, Sigma's AACFlag injects a NaN position to blind the check, and WatchdogVelocity modes apply the knockback client-side exactly as the server computes it. The companion S27PacketExplosion carries its own knockback and must be handled separately, which is why every serious module pairs S12 and S27. Rise 5.99 even ships an anticheat-side velocity recorder in dev/rise/anticheat/data/PlayerData.java and a dcOnVeloCheck disconnect in AutoHypixel that reacts to velocity-based server checks.

overview: The knockback packet: three shorts at x8000 written directly into entity motion. The most-handled clientbound packet in the 8-client corpus, spanning cancel-or-scale anti-knockback (Memeware, Nekoware, Spicy, Tenacity, Rise 5.99), per-anticheat timing suites (Sigma AAC modes, Rise 5.99 modes, the Rise 6.x ten-mode Velocity module), movement modules that use S12 as a boost trigger (GrimFlight TNT, WatchdogLongJump, WatchdogFireball, Sigma Fly), and component infrastructure (PingSpoofComponent buffers it as the velocity class).
server_handling: EntityTrackerEntry keeps lastTrackedEntityMotionX/Y/Z and sends S12 to tracked players when the entity's motion changes beyond a threshold (sendVelocityUpdates). EntityPlayer.attackEntityFrom sends S12 to the damaged player with the knockback vector from the attacker's motion. The client applies value / 8000.0 directly to motionX/Y/Z with no validation, so the packet is a trusted write into the physics state. Explosion knockback travels separately in S27 and is not covered by S12.
protocol_notes: VarInt entity id plus three shorts at x8000, no rotations, no metadata. Values are signed, so negative motion (pulled, pushed back) encodes naturally. The client divides by 8000.0 on apply; the short range limits motion to roughly -4.096 to 4.096 blocks/tick. Because the write is direct, packet order matters: an S12 arriving after the tick's movement code runs applies one tick late, which knockback-timing modules exploit.
anticheat_landscape: Velocity checks reconcile the knockback vector with the player's reported position over the following ticks. Cancelling S12 is instantly measurable, so modern modes instead cancel selectively (first N packets, then pass one), reverse the vector (Sigma AACPush converts it into a strafe boost), or replay the exact server motion (WatchdogVelocity). Grim and Vulcan are sensitive to delayed application, which is why Rise 6.x splits the Velocity module into per-anticheat modes (GrimVelocity, VulcanVelocity, MMCVelocity, RedeskyVelocity, UniversoCraftVelocity, WatchdogPredictionVelocity) and why Rise 5.99's own anticheat records S12 in PlayerData.java for its checks.

modules.name: Velocity / AntiKnockback (cancel and scale)
modules.purpose: Remove or scale knockback by intercepting the S12 that targets the local player.
modules.how_it_works: A packet-receive handler checks the entity id; if it matches the player, the packet is cancelled outright (Memeware, Nekoware, Rise 5.99 at 0% settings) or its motion fields are scaled by horizontal/vertical percentages (Spicy, Tenacity). S27PacketExplosion is cancelled or scaled in the same handler because explosion knockback bypasses S12.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Outright cancellation is the fastest flag on any velocity-check anticheat; scaling to a nonzero percentage passes on servers that only check for complete absence of motion. Rise 5.99's Custom mode layers timer and attack-time scaling to blur the cancel.
modules.variations: Memeware and Nekoware are byte-for-byte the same cancel logic. Spicy scales via settings and cancels S27 always. Tenacity scales via NumberSettings and cancels both packets at 0%. Rise 5.99 adds modes (Reverse, Ground, Stack, Follow First Tick) on top of the same Custom scale. November Recode 2.0's VelocityModule is the same-role module with per-mode scaling (REDUCE, REVERSE) and anticheat-specific cancels (GRIM, VULCAN, WATCHDOG_SAFE).

modules.name: AntiVelocity (Sigma AAC modes)
modules.purpose: Defeat knockback with anticheat-specific tricks instead of a plain cancel.
modules.how_it_works: Basic mode scales or cancels S12 and cancels S27. AACPush samples the knockback vector, cancels the packet and turns the stored motion into a decaying strafe boost over 10 ticks. AACFlag cancels the packet and injects a C04 with NaN Y while the player is in hurt time, desyncing the anticheat's position model.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket (registerEvent with EventUpdate), pre stage for clientbound.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The AACFlag NaN-position injection is a hostile desync that several 1.8 anti-cheats mis-handle; it is also the most detectable pattern in the module when the server sanity-checks NaN coordinates. AACPush keeps motion nonzero, which defeats simple knockback-absence checks.
modules.variations: The module also guards Sigma's own BowFly: when Fly is in BowFly mode the S12 for the player is left intact so the bow-boost velocity is preserved.

modules.name: Velocity / Rise 6.x suite (per-anticheat modes)
modules.purpose: Per-anticheat anti-knockback: ten modes in the Velocity module, each tuned to a specific server anticheat.
modules.how_it_works: Each mode is a Mode subclass of the Velocity module handling PacketReceiveEvent: StandardVelocity scales/cancels and optionally copies the server's vertical motion into motionY; GrimVelocity, VulcanVelocity, MMCVelocity, RedeskyVelocity and UniversoCraftVelocity tune cancellation and replay timing per anticheat; WatchdogVelocity and WatchdogPredictionVelocity emulate the knockback the Watchdog check expects; BufferAbuseVelocity and LegitVelocity delay or minimize application. The onSwing gate skips handling unless the player is swinging, which hides the module's presence during combos.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketReceiveEvent, PreMotionEvent, TeleportEvent; packet replaced via event.setPacket.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: The suite's core trick is not cancelling but reshaping: rescale the packet and re-set it so the pipeline delivers a modified but present velocity, then let one tick of real knockback through. The commented-out Watchdog strafe logic in StandardVelocity shows the iteration history of the mode.
modules.variations: 6.2.4 adds WatchdogPredictionVelocity to the 6.1.30 lineup; the mode set otherwise matches (Grim, Legit, MMC, Redesky, Standard, UniversoCraft, Vulcan, Watchdog, BufferAbuse).

modules.name: Flight / LongJump (movement boost)
modules.purpose: Use the player's own S12 as a trigger or fuel for flight and longjump acceleration.
modules.how_it_works: Flight and longjump modes listen for S12 targeting the player and either flip a state flag that enables teleport-style flight (GrimFlight TNT), buffer the velocity for a follow-up boost (WatchdogLongJump, WatchdogFireball), or scale it into movement acceleration (Sigma Fly, Tenacity FlightModule). The packet is deliberately not cancelled, because the anti-cheat expects the knockback motion to exist.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: These modes are the flip side of anti-knockback: they need the S12 to arrive intact, so they must not conflict with the Velocity module, and they exploit the fact that the server cannot distinguish a knockback-boosted jump from a legitimate one when the packet was never tampered with.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99 uses S12 in Fly Minemenclub and LongJump Hycraft/Vulcan; Rise 6.x spreads it across GrimFlight, MatrixFlight, MineLandFlight, WatchdogFlight, WatchdogJesus, WatchdogLongJump, WatchdogBowLongJump, WatchdogFireball, NCPSpeed and WatchdogSpeed; Sigma handles it inside Fly; Tenacity inside FlightModule.

modules.name: PingSpoofComponent (velocity buffer)
modules.purpose: Delay S12 alongside transactions and keepalives while ping spoofing, which delays knockback application as a side effect.
modules.how_it_works: The component classifies packets into tuples: S12 is grouped with S27 in the velocity tuple. While a spoof is active, matching packets are cancelled from the event stream and parked in a timestamped queue; onPostMotion flushes entries whose delay elapsed via PacketUtil.queue, which bypasses the event bus. The players tuple holds S13 and the S14/S18/S19/S20 entity stream so entity ordering survives the buffering.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Delayed S12 is safe against velocity checks that sample a single tick (the knockback still arrives), but dangerous against checks that measure the gap between the hit and the motion, which is why the component is paired with per-anticheat Velocity modes in the same client.
modules.variations: Identical component in 6.1.30 and 6.2.4; 6.2.4's PingSpoof and Timer modules both drive it via the static spoof() entry points.

modules.name: VelocityModule (per-anticheat modes)
modules.purpose: Per-mode anti-knockback: scale, reverse or cancel S12 for the local player, with anticheat-specific transaction handling for Grim and Vulcan.
modules.how_it_works: The packet listener ignores S12 whose entity id is not the local player, then switches on mode. REDUCE and REVERSE scale the motion fields in place with horizontal and vertical percentages and REVERSE negates the result; CANCEL, GRIM and VULCAN cancel the event; INTAVE and WATCHDOG are TODO stubs; WATCHDOG_SAFE cancels then re-applies only the vertical component to motionY while on the ground. GRIM mode additionally buffers S32 confirm-transaction actions and cancels the matching C0F echo on the send side; VULCAN cancels a single C0F echo after the first knockback.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: In-place scaling is the stealthiest path; outright cancel is the fastest flag on any velocity check. The GRIM transaction buffer exists because Grim correlates the S32/C0F gap with knockback, so the module hides both at once; the WATCHDOG_SAFE vertical re-apply keeps the server's expected motion curve while zeroing horizontal drift.
modules.variations: Memeware and Nekoware cancel with no modes; Rise 6.x splits per-anticheat handling across Mode subclasses of the Velocity module; November packs the modes into one class with transaction buffering built in.

general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent is universal; the packet is re-set on the event in Rise (event.setPacket) and mutated or cancelled in place on classic event buses (Memeware, Nekoware, Sigma, Spicy). Rise 6.x handles it through the component system and the Velocity module's Mode classes.
client_variations: Memeware/Nekoware cancel inside PacketInEvent; Spicy mutates the packet object and cancels the event; Tenacity cancels or scales via IEventListener; Rise 5.99 replaces the packet on the event; Rise 6.x re-sets it and additionally buffers it in PingSpoofComponent; Sigma mutates or cancels and injects C04 for the AACFlag mode. November Recode 2.0 cancels or mutates the packet inside EventPacket.In and additionally hooks C0F sends for the GRIM and VULCAN transaction games.
